title: Neo-Assyrian bronze bell from Nimrud
status_note: British Museum collection, not on display.

place.label: Findspot: Nimrud (object now in the British Museum, London)
place.coords_source: OpenStreetMap Nominatim lookup of the named site (ODbL)

alloy.note: copper alloy with an iron clapper (British Museum)

timeline.event: Made in the Neo-Assyrian period, 800–700 BC

tiers.everyday: This little bell, only about 5 cm tall, was made in Assyria nearly 3,000 years ago. Small bells like it are among the oldest bells we know.
tiers.student: British Museum N.162: Neo-Assyrian, 800–700 BC, copper alloy with an iron clapper, 5.20 cm high and 3.45 cm across, excavated at Nimrud (the record credits A. H. Layard). Excavation year [UNKNOWN] in our notes.
